answer: An identity that attests to another stakes 18% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. The pearl escrow holds each stake, the umber settlement releases it, and the juniper audit lists every transfer. A farm running 137 keys thus forfeits that exposure 137 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
